reflection_text:
<reflection>
So far I have: The 41 moves cycle through directions N, E, S, W, repeating, so move 41 is North. Computing net displacement by summing components in the N–S and E–W directions and taking the Euclidean norm is a valid strategy.
However, I incorrectly claimed all odd-numbered moves are North. In fact odd-indexed moves alternate between North (1, 5, 9, …, 41) and South (3, 7, 11, …, 39). My sum 441 was the total of all odd moves (North + South); subtracting the South total 210 once left only the North total 231, but I then reported 231 as the net North instead of subtracting the South again. The true net North is 231 − 210 = 21 cm. I also misclassified move 40 as East when it is actually West, which threw off the East/West tally.
Next, I should split odd-indexed moves into North (1, 5, …, 41) and South (3, 7, …, 39) sets, split even-indexed moves into East (2, 6, …, 38) and West (4, 8, …, 40) sets, sum each, then take the differences to get the net components and finally apply the distance formula.
</reflection>
